name: Oprah Winfrey
profession: Talk Show Host, Television Producer & Media Mogul
bio: Oprah Gail Winfrey is an American talk show host, television producer, actress, author, and philanthropist best known for her nationally syndicated talk program, The Oprah Winfrey Show, which broadcast for 25 seasons from 1986 to 2011. Dubbed the 'Queen of All Media', she became North America's first multi-billionaire Black woman and modernized the confessional television talk genre. Through Oprah's Book Club and the Oprah Winfrey Network (OWN), she remains one of the world's most influential cultural tastemakers.

faq.q: How long did The Oprah Winfrey Show run on television?
faq.a: It aired nationally for 25 seasons from September 8, 1986 to May 25, 2011, producing 4,561 episodes.
The term refers to the enormous commercial surge and cultural influence when Oprah endorses a book, company, product, or candidate.

name: David Letterman
profession: Late-Night Talk Show Host, Comedian & Producer
bio: David Michael Letterman is an American television host, comedian, writer, and producer who hosted late-night television talk shows for 33 consecutive years (1982–2015). Beginning with Late Night with David Letterman on NBC and continuing with Late Show with David Letterman on CBS, his subversive wit, meta-humor, Top Ten lists, and quirky segments fundamentally revolutionized the talk show format. Since 2018, he has hosted the in-depth interview series My Next Guest Needs No Introduction on Netflix.

famousWorks.title: Debut of Late Night with David Letterman on NBC
Launch of Late Show with David Letterman on CBS

awards: Mark Twain Prize for American Humor (2017)

faq.q: How many total late-night episodes did David Letterman host?
faq.a: Letterman hosted 6,080 late-night talk show episodes, surpassing Johnny Carson as the longest-serving late-night talk show host in American television history.

faq.q: What were signature recurring segments on Letterman's show?
faq.a: Famous segments included the 'Top Ten List', 'Stupid Pet Tricks', and throwing objects off the roof of the Ed Sullivan Theater.
